newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar's Rasgas set to start drilling.
newsitem.headline: Qatar's Rasgas set to start drilling.

text.p: Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG company (Rasgas) will start drilling the first two North Field wells in its five million tonnes a year project by the end of March, a company official said on Saturday.

"We will start drilling the first two wells by the end of this month, eight more by the end of next year and five others in the third quarter of 1999," Neil Kelly, the company's managing director, told reporters.
David Wright, Rasgas logistics superintendent, said two rigs would be brought in from Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates later this month to launch the operations.
Rasgas, is one of the oil and gas-rich state's three multi-billion-dollar gas projects to tap its North Field reserves -- the world's largest single concentration of gas.

Rasgas, which is designed eventually to produce 10 million tonnes a year, is 66.5 percent owned by the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC), 26.5 percent by U.S. Mobil Corp, four percent by Nissho Iwai and three percent by Itochu Corp.
Rasgas has signed a sale-and-purchase agreement with Seoul's Korea Gas Corporation (KGC) to supply 4.8 million tonnes a year of LNG for 25 years from mid 1999.
